environment.system_changes: None; used existing repository venv and CUDA toolkit. No low-precision package installed.

workload.input: TinyStoriesV2-GPT4-valid.txt, performance input only; no checkpoint produced
workload.precision: BF16 arithmetic; FP32 master weights and Adam state
workload.optimizer: fresh fused AdamW, lr 1e-5, betas .9/.95, wd .1, clipping 1.0; not restored training state or exact CLI parameter groups
workload.depth: Fixed ceiling 24 except sampled case using checkpoint mean 12.8
workload.files: Checkpoint opened read-only; optimizer updates only in RAM/VRAM.

telemetry.note: nvidia-smi observations during unprofiled timing; GPU busy is not SM/Tensor Core occupancy.

findings: Two fixed-24 exact BF16 runs: 0.4125 and 0.4158 s/update; peak 4.97-4.98 GiB.
Disabling expert checkpointing: 0.3587 and 0.3615 s/update, approximately 15% higher observed throughput; peak 16.80-17.78 GiB. This is a measured option, not a changed default.
Padded dispatch: 0.5548 s/update, slower despite fewer kernel launches. Grouped ragged GEMM is a different proposal, not what this padded path measures.
Sampled-depth baseline: median 0.3262 s/update, 12.56k processed or 6.28k new tokens/s. Depth varied; do not compare directly with fixed-24 to claim an optimization gain.
Representative exact repeat trace: 24,832 kernels and 7,495 aten::mm calls. Significant copying, Python dispatch and host synchronization accompany GEMM.

In that trace approximately 30% of expert-shaped matrix multiplications have fewer than 128 rows. Padding each independently to 128 would add about 10.3% matmul row work in aggregate; quantization/launch overhead remains additional.

quartet_ii_review.supported_hardware: README explicitly supplies RTX 5090 sm120a kernels; CMake defaults include 100a,120a,103a.
quartet_ii_review.tested_stack_claim: CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.10, Python 3.11; our newer stack has not been tested with it.
quartet_ii_review.backend: Current linear.py uses FlashInfer mm_fp4 with cuDNN; CUDA quantization kernels and a custom backward.
quartet_ii_review.shape_requirement: quant_fp4 asserts both dimensions divisible by 128. Expert widths 512/2048 satisfy this; routed token counts need handling.
quartet_ii_review.parameter_integration: Paged experts use slab parameters and functional matmuls, so replacing nn.Linear modules alone misses the main expert workload.
quartet_ii_review.causality_risk: Source review: default input_amax=abs_max(flat_input) spans token rows. Future activations can therefore affect prefix quantization scales. A causal/static calibration policy and prefix/chunk tests are prerequisites; this has not been tested with the Quartet kernels locally.
quartet_ii_review.quality: Paper studies forward and backward NVFP4 with improved gradient estimation; it does not validate this recurrent, hard-routed/halting model.

recommendation: Optimize BF16 host/device transfers, synchronization and expert dispatch based on this profile; evaluate checkpointing as a configurable per-workload choice.
Microbenchmark FP8 and Quartet II NVFP4 forward+backward on observed expert shapes, including quantization, padding and launch overhead. Generic SM120/a/f flags alone are not an optimization.
Retain FP32 master weights/optimizer state and higher precision for routing, halting, norms and losses; test selective lower precision in expert GEMMs.

Require causal scaling, unchanged prefix behavior, checkpoint/optimizer ownership checks, and matched-data/depth-schedule training comparisons scored with predictive CE. Judge wall time to equivalent quality, not peak FLOPS alone.
limitations: Few-step single-corpus, single-GPU measurement; cache-warmed runs, not sustained full-corpus throughput. Initial loading, growth/pruning, evaluation and checkpoint saves are excluded.

CUDA/BF16 nondeterminism and finite-precision dispatch differences produced different learning/routing trajectories between runs. Comparisons are observations, not a mathematical equivalence or convergence result.
Profiler overhead: exact instrumented step about 511 ms vs unprofiled median about 416 ms. Event times cannot be used as an exact unprofiled Amdahl bound.
Profiler operator/device sums may overlap; kernel union is separate from SM occupancy, memory bandwidth, or Tensor Core utilization. Nsight hardware counters were not measured.
FLOP accounting is incomplete; no model FLOP utilization percentage is claimed.
Quartet II was reviewed, not installed/built/benchmarked. No FP8/NVFP4 speed or convergence result for mini-AGI is claimed.
